title: Conversational Persian tone pass
description: A story-wide consistency pass that makes the Persian text conversational, clear, and friendly while preserving the source meaning and scene order.
style_guide: Use natural contemporary conversational Persian in both narration and character dialogue.
Avoid formal written forms such as می‌باشد، می‌شود، می‌توان، می‌خواهد and formal object marker را where a natural spoken form is appropriate.
Prefer common spoken forms such as می‌شه، می‌تونه، می‌خواد، می‌دونه، اون، اونا and رو.
Keep the prose literary and restrained; do not turn it into exaggerated slang.
Preserve names, facts, emotional meaning, story order, scene pacing, and source-specific terminology.

review_scope.method: Effective translation layers were merged in the same precedence order used by the app, then revised entries were added as a final overlay. Four event-alignment errors in the previous final review layer were corrected against the English source.

She smiled for me as if she were flying, as if she were delighted,
as if she were an honest-to-god bikini model ...
